conversion_warnings: CREDIT SYSTEM: Bowdoin counts in full-credit courses, not credit-hours. 32 courses are required to graduate, each = 1 unit. Modeled as system_type=semester, credit_hours=1.0 per course, total_credits=32.
degree_type corrected to BA: Bowdoin awards only the Bachelor of Arts (AB); the skeletal source said BS. CS major name is 'Computer Science Major (AB)'.

Major = 10 CSCI courses + 1 MATH course. Core (4): (CSCI 2100 or CSCI 2101) + CSCI 2102 + CSCI 2200 + CSCI 2330. Electives (5): ≥1 theory, ≥1 systems, ≥1 AI, ≥1 projects, with ≥2 of the five at the 3000-level. Plus one MATH course numbered 1300+.
The intro course CSCI 1101/1103 does NOT count toward the major (students placing into CSCI 2100/2101 skip it); modeled CSCI 1101/1103 only as a prerequisite of CSCI 2101, not as a major requirement.
The 'choose one' core entry is modeled as a select count:1 over {CSCI 2100, CSCI 2101}; CSCI 2100 is the accelerated single-course equivalent of CSCI 1101 + CSCI 2101.

The four named-category electives (theory/AI/systems/projects) use exclude_used:true so the same course does not satisfy two categories. CSCI 3225/3325/3465/3485/3725 appear in multiple category pools per the catalogue (e.g. 3225 counts for both theory and projects).

'≥2 of the five electives must be 3000-level' is only partially enforceable across separate select blocks: the four category picks already include several 3000-level options and the 'Additional CS elective' block carries min_upper_division:1. Full joint enforcement of the 2-at-3000 rule across all five picks is not expressible in the schema and is documented here.

Prerequisites deep-traced from the Bowdoin CSCI course catalogue (catalogue.bowdoin.edu / bowdoin-public.courseleaf.com/courses/csci). Grade-of-C- prereq qualifiers omitted from boolean expressions for tractability (degree-level grade_minimum applies). Placement/MATH co-prereqs for intro courses omitted as they are non-CSCI gating, not major requirements.
MATH1300 is a placeholder course defined to back the 'MATH:1300+' pool (one math course 1300+); the catalogue does not fix a single course, so any MATH 1300+ satisfies it.

Bowdoin distribution requirement modeled as five separate gen_ed select blocks (DPI, INS, IP, MCSR, VPA), each one full-credit course, plus the First-Year Writing Seminar. All marked external_requirement:true with '*:*' pools because they are attribute-based and not enumerable from the defined course set (PatternMatchesNoCourses avoidance).

MCSR distribution can be (and typically is) satisfied by a CSCI or MATH course that also counts for the major; this double-count is allowed for distribution but not modeled, slightly inflating the standalone distribution credit count.
cip_code 11.0701 (Computer Science) inferred from program name; not stated in catalogue.

Credit reconciliation: major+math = 10 courses, first-year seminar = 1, five distribution areas = 5, free electives = 16 -> 10+1+5+16 = 32 courses total. Exact free-elective count varies with distribution/major overlap (MCSR commonly satisfied by a major course), which would raise free electives; the schema double-counting policy is allow_double_counting-absent so distribution is modeled as additive.
